Hello and this is my first post!

I play deadlock 2 with some frequency and find all the guides on the internet lacking in information which would help the players. So here are the short tips/tricks/etc listed. You can add more, if you know some and i will post them here and in the comments subsequently.

  • In the start and in general gameplay(for example, start with 4 colonists and techs are not researched), i advise to build houses first(2-3 houses in the first turn). The reason is that when you have more room for expansion(population), the bigger the population growth. The population growth is defined by terrain(marsh and mountain are the slowest while plains are the fastest) and how big is the % of current population/max population(defined by built houses and showed in the right top corner). I don't remember the exact %, but for example - the first turn it goes up 12%, since you have 400 colonists and max is 1000(depending on scenario, but i will choose 1000 now). On the next turn, the player built 3 more houses and the max pop jumps to 2500. The player have now 448 colonists(12% more). Since 448/2500 is now 17.92%(from the 40% in the first turn; 400/1000), the growth(%) will be now bigger. It becomes 16-18% per turn. This will give the player a headstart in population and subsequently taxes. From there it is now a preference, if the player wants to upgrade those houses or go build other things, though in my personal experience, second turn should be spent on upgrading those houses. Having more than 4 houses isn't advised, because of the maximum population per area(5k) and every house can be upgraded to hold 1.5k, so two max upgraded houses and 2 mid level houses is enough. The other areas should also prioritize in housing buildings as soon as they are colonized. 1-2 will do.

  • Expanding on the first point - since in the long run population will always grow faster, it is important to get the museum up because of the overpopulation unhappiness. You can't build the museum directly, you have to build the cultural center first and then upgrade it. Depending on the scenario, it takes 3-4 turns to upgrade it with 4-5 colonists(depending on the scenario, normal production or boosted production). It is advisable to build this building on turn 6-7. In general terms - Marsh and mountains get overpopulation unhappiness starting from the 1k, forests about 1.1-1.2k, plains get from 1.5k. So for example with previous housing strategy plains would get morale hit at about turn 10. Transporting colonists to another area can alleviate this.

  • Getting wood is as important as food, because houses need 10 wood, cultural centers need 25 wood and surface mines need 50 wood. In general, you get 75 wood from the start and it's not enough to build all the starting buildings(first 10 turns). Usually the starting wood goes to housing and first cultural center. The farm should be built on turn 2-4(depending on the desired aggressiveness of population growth and the planetary resources). The first turns on the farm should be spent on wood, not food.

  • Don't worry about the minuses in the resource boxes if you know what you are doing. For example, food is not important until turn 6-7 when it starts to run out. Surplus food doesn't give you anything. You should keep it low, depending on the current population(small buffer is needed, though). The only time you need bigger buffer of food is when you upgrade your farms.

  • Transporting the resources to other areas, before the tech which reduces transportation costs, is very costly, but can be efficiently mitigated in only some places. Example - Getting wood for cultural centre or surface mine on the second area is advisable. When you build buildings, the transportation cost of the materials is added. After the transportation tech specialization of areas is more achievable.

  • Defense is important, but this can be delayed depending on the scenario. If the opponent has no starting military, it is recommended to build the defense on areas on turns 10-15. Starting from there, every front area(not inner) should have defense up asap. From turns 20-25, the fronts should have 2 defense buildings and later also a flak.

  • Morale. The starting morale is 100. When morale goes below 91, there will be population which can't be used(rebels/rioters). The lower, the worse. Those upper 10 points of morale is important to capitalize(through taxation), but should never go below 91. For example - From the first area, when you have surplus workers(even 1; and only advisable when the first upgrades are done on all houses), put that worker on culture(city center). This will generate 2 morale per worker. Then increase taxation for this area, this will decrease morale by 5. From the 100, it will go 97. Next turn reduce the taxation to normal. This will increase morale from 97-99. What you achieved is more money from the first turn. Depending on the desired aggresiveness, this tactic should be always used. In the first area(where you have city center), it is more profitable to do culture than trade. On other areas, it depends on population - more population -> bigger the taxation -> more profitable morale manipulation.

Museum helps a lot - you can increase taxation two steps in the short run(increase overall taxation, then increase taxation for this specific area and decrease taxation for all other areas).

Also, some military units can suppress population and thus increase morale. I don't remember exactly which ones can do that, but fusion cannon increases morale by 7(if i remember correctly). Since military costs go up exponentially, it is not advised to build more than 2-3 tanks and 3-4 troopers.

Endurium mining is also very important to research because of morale - This gives a building called art complex, where you can build art artifacts(sp?). With 4 colonists, the production will be 0.75-1 per turn(depending on race and production settings in scenario). Every one of them will give +2 morale. Only 5 can give an effect for an area, thus giving +10 morale. Having more than 5 in an area will not produce more morale. Very important for marsh and mountain areas, since their overpopulation hit for 5k population is -20. Also for city center areas for increased taxation.

  • City center doubles the taxation income for the area where it is built. Even in purely conquest scenarios, it is advisable to build a second city center(with morale manipulation it will be a big income). Next city centers are less profitable.

  • Tax per population is not linear. It is more profitable to have more areas, but less population per area, than having one area with maximum population(also the overpopulation hit). Without city center, default taxation and 5k population an area will produce 100-104 money. First colonist(100 population) with default tax will produce 14 money(if i remember correctly). 1k will produce about 50. With morale tactics, it's common to see 100 tax with 1k population and then with overpopulation the tax will stay same since that.

  • With the population growth gotten from the first point, it is recommended to build the low tech buildings first and then upgrade them. This way you have more money left for other buildings and further expansion. Low tech buildings need only wood and iron.

  • Steel is very important 50% through the game. Converting an iron to steel will net 4 'metal' profit, since 1 steel is 5 iron. Transportation costs will also be reduced. For example, a building needs 50 iron. Transporting this from other areas will cost(after transportation tech - hoverway) 50 money. Transporting steel will cost only 10 money. Before hoverway - double the cost. It is strongly recommended to create a factory(to create steel) in the area where you mine the metal. Endurium will give an option to create metal in other areas to reduce transportation costs, but even after that iron and endurium should be 50/50, even if steel and endurium are same in value.

  • What to mine, endurium or iron. Examples - When you can mine 20 iron or 10 endurium(that is equivalent to 50 iron) and resources are scarce, it is more advisable to mine iron, because 20 iron can be converted to 20 steel, which is equivalent to 100 iron. When money is more important, then it is advisable to hold 3-4x rule - 30-40 iron, 10 endurium. Over time, it is more advisable to go endurium route since metal will be more plentiful(except on aggressive offense strategies) and factories can also give trade. Tridium processing(converts from endurium and doubles the value; 1 tridium is 10 iron) will almost eliminate iron mining.

  • Not all workers are the same. Specifically, not all workplaces are the same. Example - automated factory can hold 6 workers. In boosted scenario - Putting 1 worker to steel conversion will give 6 steel, 2 workers 12 steel, 3 workers 18 steel, 4 workers 22 steel, 5 workers 28 steel and 6 workers 30 steel(or 32, don't remember). The last worker will always give less production than others(that is, when producing only 1 product), so it is advisable to put workers on other things to work(same building or other buildings). Also, notice that the 4th worker produces only 4 steel instead of usual 6(that's already 10 iron difference). So it's more usual to see 3 workers in trade and 3 on steel. Or 5 steel and 1 trade if metal is more needed. All workplaces are affected by these variations.
